eventMetadata.context_description: Orlando Magic hold a 3-2 series lead over the top-seeded Detroit Pistons in their NBA playoffs first-round matchup, with Game 6 tonight at Kia Center putting Detroit's season on the line. Magic forward Franz Wagner is out with a right calf strain after exiting Game 5 early, severely impacting their scoring alongside Paolo Banchero, while Jonathan Isaac remains doubtful with a left knee sprain. Pistons list Tobias Harris (left ankle) and Kevin Huerter (left adductor) as questionable, though Cade Cunningham's 45-point, playmaking explosion in Game 5's 116-109 win—matching Banchero's output—fuels momentum. Orlando's elite defense and home-court edge contrast Detroit's regular-season dominance (60-22) and desperation drive toward a potential Game 7 at Little Caesars Arena.

eventMetadata.context_description: France holds a narrow edge in trader consensus at 16.4% implied probability to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup, closely trailed by Spain at 15.3%, as both nations wrapped dominant qualification campaigns with unbeaten records in UEFA groups and showcased attacking flair in March friendlies—France's 3-1 win over Colombia highlighting Mbappé's form. The tight race stems from an expanded 48-team field with group stage advancement for top two plus eight best third-placed teams, favoring squad depth over single stars; Spain's Euro 2024 champions benefit from Yamal and young midfielders in a Group H with Uruguay, while France faces Haaland-led Norway in Group I. England, Argentina, and Brazil lag slightly due to tougher draws and aging cores like Messi, underscoring upset potential in knockout rounds.

eventMetadata.context_description: In Game 6 of their Eastern Conference first-round playoff series—with Cleveland holding a 3-2 lead—the Cavaliers face elimination pressure on the road at Scotiabank Arena against a resilient Raptors squad fighting for a Game 7. Toronto's momentum stems from their Game 5 road victory three days ago, where Scottie Barnes delivered 14 points and 10 assists by halftime of the latest matchup, showcasing his two-way impact alongside RJ Barrett. Both teams enter with clean injury reports, headlined by Barnes' availability and no major concerns for Donovan Mitchell or James Harden; Cleveland's superior regular-season form and playoff experience drive trader consensus, though Toronto's home crowd, desperation, and defensive intensity on Harden pose upset risks in this closeout opportunity.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Negotiations for a US-Iran permanent peace deal remain stalled after Tehran submitted a new proposal via Pakistani mediators, offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities in exchange for lifting the US blockade, but President Trump rejected it Friday as insufficient without ironclad nuclear non-proliferation commitments. A Phase 1 ceasefire took hold in early April following US airstrikes that dismantled Iranian air defenses, petrochemical facilities, and IRGC assets, paving the way for Phase 2 talks in Islamabad on sanctions relief, nuclear curbs, reparations, and regional security guarantees. Vice President Vance's marathon sessions ended without accord as Iran decoupled war cessation from atomic pledges, heightening tensions ahead of potential escalation or diplomatic breakthroughs by late May.

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil futures retreated 2.45% to $102.50 for the June 2026 contract on May 1 amid trader hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire easing Strait of Hormuz disruptions, trimming gains from wartime highs near $109 earlier in the week driven by prolonged supply fears. OPEC+ approved a symbolic 206,000 barrels per day output hike for May, countering robust US production at 13.6 million bpd plateau, while EIA forecasts global inventory builds and softening demand growth to 0.6 million bpd in 2026, capping upside. Polymarket traders price near-certainty for intraday highs above $105 already achieved this month, with elevated risks for dips below $95; watch weekly EIA inventories Wednesdays and IEA Oil Market Report on May 13 for demand cues.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Gavin Newsom as the clear frontrunner for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination at 26%, reflecting his commanding leads in recent national primary polls like McLaughlin's April survey and sustained national visibility from a New Hampshire book tour earlier this year, positioning him as a battle-tested California governor with robust fundraising. Kamala Harris trails at 11% despite hints of another run amid post-2024 travels, weighed by her recent loss and uneven polling recovery, while Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's 8% stems from strong youth support in Yale and Emerson surveys. Jon Ossoff's recent surge to 6% highlights Georgia's battleground appeal. Consolidation could hinge on 2026 midterm results for governors like Shapiro and Whitmer, progressive vs. moderate faction endorsements, and early-state organizing ahead of the 2028 primaries.
